note: Clean pass with caveats. Source is the EANNA 2023 deposit itself (BIDAT dataset e3ceb7aa-95a8-4838-909b-155719847d21, licence 'Creative Commons Attribution', published by Chile's Ministerio de Desarrollo Social y Familia; fieldwork by INE). Two deposit documents were used and they answer different questions: the codebook 'Libro de codigos base de datos EANNA 2023' (sha256 0478c51b7101a71a5a70f1219f1d17e4752f9cff1d0e50ab98118e02e547306a), sheet '4. NNA', ties every variable NAME to a variable label and to value labels with frequencies -- that is the MAPPING; and the administered questionnaire PDF 'Cuestionario_Ninos_Ninas_y_Adolescentes_9_a_17_anos_EANNA_2023.pdf' (sha256 567e0c0ddcb6dd64b61b8bd43ec5a0e2d97af20f7f03458678a88aeedc9b6766) carries the full Spanish wording read to respondents -- that is the WORDS. The codebook's variable labels are abbreviated forms of the questionnaire's stems (e.g. a5_2 is labelled 'Algun profesor envio mensaje o te contacto para saber por que faltaste colegio' against the administered 'La ultima vez que faltaste, alguno de tus profesores(as) te envio un mensaje o te contacto a ti o a tu apoderado, madre o padre para saber por que faltaste al colegio?'), so the shipped item_text is the questionnaire's, not the label's. (1) data/chile_2023_children-adolescents-survey.do writes `gen item = "`var'"`, so `item` IS the source Stata variable name -- the exempt code-derivation pattern -- and mapping_basis is data_labels. It was checked against the data anyway, by route 9: 81 of 83 item x value cells reproduce the codebook's published frequencies exactly, the two exceptions (a11_2 resp=1 codebook 395 vs live 394; a11_77 resp=0 codebook 11975 vs live 11974) being off by one respondent and internally inconsistent in the codebook itself (those two variables sum to 12424 where every other a11_* sums to 12423). All 38 frequency profiles are distinct, so the route distinguishes every item from every other, including inside the a8_*/a9_*/a11_* blocks whose per-item n are identical. (2) Shape: a8, a9 and a11 are multiple-select questions stored as one 0/1 column per alternative, so their shared stem is in section_prompt and each alternative's wording is the item_text; option_text is the codebook's own 0='No' / 1='Si'. The seven single-select questions (a3, a5_1-a5_3, a6, a10, a12) each get a trivial one-question section with a blank section_prompt. (3) Nine shipped items are not substantive content: a8_78/a8_87/a8_88/a8_99, a9_78/a9_87/a9_88/a9_99 and a11_88/a11_99 are the 'A nadie' / 'No aplica' / 'No sabe' / 'No responde' checkboxes of those same multiple-select questions, which the do-file's mvdecode pass did not touch because they are column NAMES rather than stored values. They are real response alternatives of the source instrument and are shipped as such, but a reader should not treat them as items measuring a construct. (4) Two interviewer-facing markers were stripped and are disclosed here: the questionnaire prints '78. A nadie (NO LEER)' and '87. No aplica (NO LEER)' -- (NO LEER) = do not read aloud -- and '77. Otra cosa. Especifique' for a11_77; the shipped text is 'A nadie', 'No aplica' and 'Otra cosa'. (5) The administered language is Spanish and the Spanish ships in the base fields. No English version of the questionnaire exists in the deposit, so the _translated columns are IRW's own translation (translation_source=machine_translation) and a public_note is written accordingly. (6) a6's anchor 1 is 'Muy mal' in the questionnaire and 'Muy Mal' in the codebook's value label; the questionnaire's casing ships. (7) Rights: no clause reserving a right is locatable. The instrument is the Chilean state's own survey questionnaire, published in full by the agency that owns it alongside a CC BY dataset; the codebook and questionnaire pages state no fee, no non-commercial term and no redistribution bar. No register row written (a round may never write ship/ship_with_note). (8) Step 3b: the dictionary Description ('children aged 9-17, particularly their principal activities and relationships with others') is a loose fit -- the live items are the 'Educacion y Percepcion' module of the 9-17 questionnaire (school attendance and absence, how school is going, who the child asks for help at school and at home, expected final grade, post-school plans, perceived usefulness of school). Not a mismatch of instrument, but the Description understates the education focus. (9) irw-validate reports two findings that are properties of the pre-existing response table's NAME, not of this item text, and neither is fixable here: name_length (41 characters against a 40-character intake cap) and name_charset (the hyphens in 'children-adolescents-survey'). The `table` column must reproduce the live IRW table name exactly for the join to work, so it was left as published; the five sibling chile_2023_children-adolescents-survey_* tables carry the same name shape.

Clean pass with two caveats. (1) Mapping verification is PARTIAL, not VERIFIED: the two routes available (column identity against the full-length twin file, and keying polarity from the .sav value labels) pin every item to its scale and to its keyed direction and reproduce the paper's published item-number lists 60/60, but they cannot separate two same-scale, same-keying items from each other - order within a keying class rests on Winterstein et al. (2011) Appendix A being printed in ascending original-item-number order. No per-item statistics are published for the WSS-SF, so there is no stronger route. (2) resp is the scored value (1 = schizotypy-keyed response), and the literal answer it corresponds to differs by item, so option_text is per-item 'True'/'False' rather than one shared pair; a reader assuming 1='True' throughout would misread 18 of the 60 items. CLEAN PASS WITH CAVEATS (batch_308). 120 rows, 60 items x 2 resp levels; validate_items.R --table-sets PASS on both sets (60/60 items, resp {0,1}), irw-validate clean (2 checks, nothing to report). Every item has both resp levels in the live data (min cell n=211), checked via the cached live fetch. MAPPING: mapping_basis=paper_explicit and it is a code-label match, not an order inference -- the study's own supplement (SI 1) prefixes each of the 60 items with the very code the live table uses (PY1 -> py01 ... MI15 -> mi15; the only differences are lowercasing and zero-padding, both applied by data/christensen_2018_wsssf.py, which lowercases the source header and otherwise keeps the source column name as `item` -- the exempt 'code IS the source column name' derivation). Verified anyway with data: verify_christensen_2018_wsssf_5831.R reproduces the paper's Table 1 subscale descriptives for this exact sample to two decimals on all four scales (Physical Anhedonia 2.09/2.30/0-14, Social Anhedonia 1.77/2.41/0-15, Perceptual Aberration 1.21/2.28/0-15, Magical Ideation 3.26/2.91/0-15), which is what pins the non-obvious py=Physical Anhedonia / pb=Perceptual Aberration assignment, plus a within-subscale permutation test on a priori content clusters. CAVEAT 1 (annotation stripped): SI 1 appends ' (reversed)' to the 18 reverse-keyed items. That is the authors' scoring annotation, not administered wording, so it was removed from item_text; nothing else was changed, and the items are otherwise character-for-character as SI 1 prints them. CAVEAT 2 (option_text is item-dependent, and that is deliberate): the table stores keyed scores, not raw answers. The paper states 'Each cell is either coded as one (participant i endorsed item j) or zero ... After reverse-scoring as needed, all items were scored so that higher scores reflected higher levels of schizotypy.' So resp=1 is 'True' on the 42 items SI 1 does not mark reversed and 'False' on the 18 it does. The data agree: the reversed items are ordinary pleasant experiences ('I like playing with and petting soft little kittens or puppies') and their endorsement rates run 0.036-0.276, not the ~0.9 a raw true/false coding would give. CAVEAT 3 (no instructions published): neither the OSF deposit nor the article reproduces the instruction text respondents read (the WSS were administered inside UNCG mass-screening packets), so `instructions` is NA rather than invented. section_id is the single trivial christensen_2018_wsssf_5831_1: the four subscales are a real grouping but carry no section_prompt text, and subscale membership already ships in the response table as itemcov_subscale. STEP 3b (instrument mismatch): none. 60 dichotomous items in four blocks of 15 with the prefixes py/pb/mi/sa is the WSS-SF and nothing else in this study; the subscale totals reproduce the paper's own Table 1 exactly. RIGHTS: no block, on a search that found no clause to quote. The wording IRW ships was published by the scales' own custodian -- Thomas R. Kwapil is a co-author of this paper and of the CC0 OSF deposit whose SI 1 prints all 60 items in full. The originating Chapman scales (Chapman, Chapman & Raulin 1978 Perceptual Aberration; Eckblad & Chapman 1983 Magical Ideation; Eckblad, Chapman, Chapman & Mishlove 1982 Revised Social Anhedonia; Chapman, Chapman & Raulin 1976 Physical Anhedonia) are unpublished tests that circulate by request from the authors; that is a distribution arrangement, not a stated term. Checked for a quotable restriction and found none: the NIMH RDoC self-report entry for the Perceptual Aberration Scale carries no licensing, permission or fee statement; no hexaco.org-style terms page exists for these scales; the deposit is CC0 1.0 and the article states no reuse condition on SI 1. Under SKILL.md's rule (silence is permission; a bar must be quotable) this ships. Two pages that would have settled it faster were unreachable at the time of extraction and are the honest gap in this search: libres.uncg.edu (connection refused) and the digitalcommons.unomaha / columbia.edu PMAP copies of the Winterstein et al. (2011) short-form paper and the Chapman-scales summary (Cloudflare interstitial). Nothing was written to instrument_rights_register.csv -- a round may never write a ship row.
